commentary_segments.text_raw:
The LNA is normally the
first active building block in
a receiver.
As it is connected directly
to the input pad over a
bonding wire, it receives
electrostatic discharge volt-
ages from outside.
These voltages can be
quite high (kV’s) and can
easily zap the Gate of the
input transistor. A protec-
tion device is now required.
Normally, this consists of
series resistances to the Gate
and parallel diodes to
ground. A low-resistance path is now realized for overvoltages. This is discussed in more
detail next.
commentary_segments.text: The LNA is normally the first active building block in a receiver. As it is connected directly to the input pad over a bonding wire, it receives electrostatic discharge voltages from outside. These voltages can be quite high (kV’s) and can easily zap the Gate of the input transistor. A protection device is now required. Normally, this consists of series resistances to the Gate and parallel diodes to ground. A low-resistance path is now realized for overvoltages. This is discussed in more detail next.
